newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Boiko calls for open,honest privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Boiko calls for open,honest privatisation.

text.p: Russia's new Privatisation Minister Maxim Boiko called on Thursday for honest, efficient and open privatisation in Russia and said recent sales had been legally conducted.

"Honest in that the way auctions are conducted must always be announced in advance, and the conditions must not change. Efficient, in that privatisation must raise significant revenues for the budget. The prices must be high and privatisation must bring investment into specific enterprises," he said.
Boiko was talking at his first news conference since President Boris Yeltsin appointed him on Wednesday as Deputy Prime Minister and Chairman of the State Property Fund to replace Alfred Kokh.
Many major Russian privatisations have appeared to be inside deals, benefiting a small number of well connected banks, and as a result not raising as much money for the treasury as possible.

Russia's biggest privatisation to date, the sale last month of one quarter of telecoms holding company Svyazinvest, was said by economists to be relatively fair and open, but bankers and businessmen linked with the losing bidders said the government had handled the deal in a corrupt way.
Boiko said the Svyazinvest privatisation and another controversial sale, of a controlling 38 percent stake in metals group Norilsk Nickel NKEL.RTS, had been lawful.
"I can say with certainty that this was done completely lawfully and that everything is in order here," he said.
Boiko said he did not intend to change senior officials in the State Property Committee, Russia's privatisation ministry.

He noted that he knew many of them well from his time there as chief economic adviser to the former head of the committee, Anatoly Chubais, who is now first deputy prime minister in charge of economic policy.
